insights: Adding specific stakes and numbers to long-form titles drastically improves discovery (e.g., 'at 2,000°C? The Hidden Trick' got 509 views vs. 4 views for the generic title).
The critical drop-off zone for Shorts occurs between 4.8s and 6.9s (losing 3% to 9% of viewers), indicating hooks must deliver on the title faster.
Explicit channel call-to-actions cause severe drop-offs; pointing to 'full breakdown on our channel' dropped 23.4% of viewers instantly at 38.6s.
Shorts formatted as 'news' or 'countdown' consistently hit over 1,000 views with strong retention between 59% and 68%.
'Myth vs fact' achieved the highest retention at 121% average view percentage, though data is limited to a single video.
Viewer comments are virtually non-existent across the entire channel (0 to 1 per video), confirming that current closing questions fail to drive engagement.
Shorts view counts depend almost entirely on entering the Shorts feed (83%-95% of traffic); when feed pickup fails (6% on Submarines), views stall under 60.
